title: Rigidity of coordinate-normalized ordinary orientations
statement: In the finite coefficient setting [def-pur-conventions], let f:X→Y be separated, finite type and smooth of pure relative dimension d≥0 between Noetherian finite-type k-schemes, with compactification and structure map aY:Y→Spec k. If e,e prime:omega0_f≈A_X(d)[2d] both satisfy the coordinate normalization of [def-pur-diagonal-dualizing-data], then e=e prime. This assertion tests equality and includes neither existence nor a pro-etale comparison.

proof.text: Construct the Tate normal form privately by induction on d: the zero tensor is the degree-zero coefficient unit and shift zero; at a successor, flatness of the finite Tate sheaf identifies derived tensor with ordinary tensor, the finite Tate product combines twists d and 1, and derivedTensorShiftIso adds the shifts. This identifies diagonalTwistEtale X d with the single finite Tate sheaf shifted by 2d. Transport the resulting upper bound and lower bound along this isomorphism and e to obtain source <= -2d and target >= -2d.

At each point apply the proved Smooth.exists_etale_to_affineSpace to choose affine opens U in X and V in Y and an etale map U to affine d-space over V. Compose with AffineSpace.map of V into Y and the inverse of affineTraceAffineSpaceIso Y d. The source U is affine, hence separated absolutely, so this coordinate morphism is separated without assuming Y separated. It is quasi-compact because U is Noetherian. The projection compatibility gives q p = j f; the separated finite-type composites over the Noetherian target admit compactifications. The chosen U cover X, including empty X.

Choose t,D using exists_ordinaryFiniteP1Adjunction, with the positive exponent and finite coefficient ring, and N using nonempty_etaleCompactSupportNormalization. Apply both normalization predicates to the same t,D,N,U,j,q and factorization equality. Their right sides are identical. Cancel the isomorphism diagonalEtaleLocality N j f to get equality of the pullbacks of the two inverse orientations.

The private map_eq_of_cover proves the required equality test directly. DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor_map_bijective_of_isLE_of_isGE makes H^(-2d) injective on these Hom sets. The canonical left-derived/exact pullback isomorphism and mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso transport each local equality to equality of restricted cohomology maps. Inverse image on the covering family jointly reflects sheaf isomorphisms and preserves equalizers, hence is jointly faithful. Thus the cohomology maps agree, and injectivity gives e.inv=e prime.inv. Iso.ext applied to the inverse isomorphisms and symmetry gives e=e prime. No gluing existence theorem or general faithfulness of derived restriction is used.

proof_origin.place: Canonicity paragraph, with direct cohomology equality detection on smooth coordinate opens
proof_origin.note: Complete Lean proof, with private proved Tate-normal-form and cover-equality helpers. The cohomology argument follows the existing proved helper map_eq_of_cover in Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.BundleSectionOrientationMapExt, but imports only its underlying general tools.

lean.statement:
theorem diagonalOrdinaryOrientationRigidity (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u})
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (d : ℕ) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f]
    [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y] [HasCompactification f]
    (aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType aY] [QuasiCompact aY]
    (e e' : P.diagonalOrdinaryDualizing f ≅ P.diagonalTwistEtale X d)
    (he : P.DiagonalOrientationNormalization d f aY e)
    (he' : P.DiagonalOrientationNormalization d f aY e') : e = e'
